item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is preferable because its retry-safe upload implementation is localized and thoroughly tested, while B makes a risky, explicitly forbidden global change to request-body and retry semantics. A still needs contract corrections before merge.","reasons":["A validates inputs, propagates reader failures, creates a replayable multipart body, and tests filename, field name, content, an os.File-backed retry, validation, and source-reader errors.","B refactors RawClient.Do despite the contract explicitly forbidding unrelated retry machinery changes and requiring FilesService.Add behavior to remain unchanged.","B's GetBody returns wrappers over the same mutable io.ReadSeeker rather than independent body copies, creating unsafe semantics if bodies overlap or GetBody is called more than once; failed seek probing can also leave the caller's reader at an altered offset.","B omits the required source-reader failure test and its Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than retrying content streamed from an open file."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's request, option, decoding, and error logic instead of routing the encoded body through Add as required.","It explicitly violates scope by adding association options and multipart field machinery, despite the contract saying not to add association fields or change FilesOption behavior.","It calls the new NewFileWithFields helper instead of directly reusing multipartbody.NewFile; the extra helper and tests add unnecessary surface area."],"risks_b":["It changes global RawClient behavior, including retries, Content-Length, body ownership, and closing semantics for every seekable request body.","Upload also duplicates Add rather than routing through it.","The shared-seeker GetBody implementation does not satisfy the usual expectation that each replay body is independent and can introduce races or offset corruption under redirects or concurrent consumption."]}
